utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, you entered the tent alone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the first one to enter the tent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you knew many people from Batkovic on the bus.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume these were mainly people from Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recollect whether they all crossed over to the next -- the other side?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that some of their own free will returned?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, recollect, some of these people who remained?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to enter the list of exchange from 1993. It was a document which we had -- a document with a 00563, which has been reciprocally disclosed. And I have both, the official translated version in B/C/S and the translated version into English. Perhaps it would be a good idea to put the B/C/S version on the ELMO. Can we get a number, unless there is an objection from the Prosecution for this document to be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. B/C/S version is D35/3 ter. And the English version is D35/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, I assume that this document -- you can put it in front of you. I assume you have never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the heading. Just slowly, please, in the right hand upper corner.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republika Srpska, Bosanski Samac municipality, commissioned for the exchange of arrested civilians and prisoners." Date: "29th of January, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is the day you went to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at this list and tell me whether you see your name on it. And if you do, under which number?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please read what it says.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "H. Hadzijusufovic ... nickname Nusko".

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose that was your nickname?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now please read the name of the person under number 10.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasanefendic Safet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does it say next to his name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Not declared himself. Returned."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be put on the ELMO. We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have another copy and just put it on the ELMO. The interpreters don't have the document, and they have to follow for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters for failing to submit a copy to them too. But since we had an official translation, I didn't think it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now please read the name under number 18.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mijo Radic, also known as Brada.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does it says next to his name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Has not declared himself. Returned."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he with you on the bus from Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that he was on the bus with you when you crossed over to Croatian territory?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't cross over to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 2, number 53, could you read the name.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Mirko Blaskic. Has not declared himself. Returned."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How about number 56?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasan Pistoljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you read what it says next to his name?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Declared himself negatively."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he on the bus with you from Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't coming from Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean was on the bus with you among the people who came from Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he travelling to be exchanged with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at this again. You don't have to read anything aloud. And tell us in terms of percentage, out of the 64 people on the list, how many were Croats? Not only because you knew them to be Croats, but also judging by their names. I mean, people who were Croat by ethnicity and to whom you referred as Catholics in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that there is certainly a half of Croats among these people, or about 50 per cent?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that the secondary school centre was disbanded before your exchange?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because all the Croats had been exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that only a few Croats remained?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are many of your fellow citizens, Croats, Catholics, whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, coming from Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But there were locals from Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Ijo Radic. There are people from Samac. I don't see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have only just a few more questions about the exchange. Have you returned to Samac since you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Domaljevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was reunited with my family and went to Zagreb, but occasionally I would return to Domoljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you submit a request for going abroad?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely. It was not a case of submitting a request. It was rather that my son sent me an invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And based on that invitation, you went abroad?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my daughter, myself, and my wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if they are going to get into where he is currently living, I ask that we go into closed session or at least that the transcript in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] No more questions about that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just interested in his movements after the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you had seen Tadic immediately in one of those first days outside the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Over the next seven months, you said you saw him two or three times a week.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw him with a beard, if you can tell us roughly?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He grew a nice beard later, perhaps in autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic. I notice that -- you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. You were exchanged on the 30th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the occasion of the exchange, or rather after the exchange, did you give any statements to Croatian authorities, or rather the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to the representatives of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you make a statement to the secret service of AID?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know what that is. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Prior to 1998, when you had an informal interview with representatives of the OTP, did you give any statement to anyone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only made statements during the interrogation by the Serbs. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify that? When was that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in Odzak, and when I was arrested, when I was detained in Pelagicevo, in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not making myself clear. In the period between the 30th of January, 1993, and May 1998, in that particular period, did you make any statements to anyone?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After that statement in 1998 until the time you came here to the courtroom, did you give any statements?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had interviews, but I made no official statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did you have interviews?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, that lady who came to visit in 1998, I had an interview with her. And there were a couple of more occasions later, but I never gave an official statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by later? Could you tell me roughly.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it perhaps a month later?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those were just discussions as to whether I would be prepared to come here. That's what we discussed. It has nothing to do with other statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You talked about that with that lady from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Be so kind as to tell me, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, prior to the 17th of April, 1992, were there any -- was there any ethnic tension in Samac between the three ethnic groups, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean myself, or the people of Samac in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean your general impression about your townsfolk and the general feeling in Samac, the atmosphere prior to the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about some skirmishes, but no, not really. All of my friends were actually Serbs; most of them, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you said that in terms of ethnic tension, prior to the 17th of April, 1992, the situation was stable in Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in my opinion. Not quite, but in the circles in which I moved, in my environment, that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You are familiar, are you not, with the term "Republika Srpska"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did you first learn about or hear of that term?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you be a little more precise? When during the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you name the month, the year?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What do you know about Republika Srpska? At that time, what did you know, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to object where we're leading with this. I mean, it's also a very vague question. If you ask me, what do you know about the United States? I mean, you can talk for seven weeks on something, or days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge in April 1992 about the fact that Republika Srpska had been established, including the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the story that made the rounds. That's what we heard. But that was because the Serbs had seized power.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that you did know about Republika Srpska in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we cannot. That cannot be my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know about certain regulations that were effective at that time in Republika Srpska, in April 1992, that applied to all the citizens of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know about the existence of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they called themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please give me a precise answer. You heard about it, and you had knowledge about it. Don't tell me that that's what they call themselves. That's not what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you see, after the 17th of April, 1992, large numbers of Serb refugees in the hundreds and maybe thousands, who had arrived from the environs of Samac into the town of Samac itself?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only the population of one village had come, from the Gradacac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date. That village was called Serbian Srnice. It was near Gradacac, and the people had moved from there into Samac. More precisely, they had moved into the Hasic village, and they put up a board of some kind saying "Serbian Srnice" in front of the Hasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was that in summer 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that all Croatian villages were abandoned at that time. It must have been earlier. Perhaps it was May. I can't really tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about any reason why the Serbs from the Srnice village had come to Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To assist the Trial Chamber about the Gradacac municipality and the village of Srnice, how far is that from Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a village located at the entrance into the town of Gradacac. Perhaps 15 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To the south of Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the south of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To make it clearer to the Trial Chamber, when you say "they" in Gradacac, who was in power in Gradacac in that region?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the people of Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who controlled that area? Whose forces? Is that a Serbian area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it Croatian?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are various villages. Srnice is Serb --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please be precise. Was Gradacac in Serb, Croat, or Muslim hands?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims lived in Gradacac. It was in Muslim hands, if you want to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that from Odzak, Novi Grad, and Dubica, in May and June, Serbs were expelled and came to Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about it from those people. I know some of them. My brother-in-law was married in Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I suppose we can agree about one fact: You have already replied to certain questions asked by the Prosecutor and one of my colleagues that this area is outside of Samac and that Muslim forces had expelled Serb citizens who later arrived to Samac.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in comparison, this transfer of Serbs from Serbian Srnice was almost humane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't remember him ever testifying to that that Muslim forces expelled Serb citizens who later arrived at Samac. That's what he said. And you said that -- I'm sorry. You've already replied to questions asked by the Prosecutor and one of my colleagues that the areas outside Samac and that Muslim forces expelled Serb citizens who later arrived to Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's a mistake in translation. I actually asked him about Croatian force, but it was not correctly reported in the transcript, so I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we will agree that you have knowledge that Croatian forces had expelled Serbs from the territory of Odzak, Dubica, Novi Grad, and that they had come to Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When testifying in front of this Trial Chamber, the Prosecutor asked you what is the 4th Detachment? You answered that in your view, it's a paramilitary formation. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After that, he also questioned -- raised a question whether the 4th Detachment was linked to any party, and you answered as yes.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then that colleague Prosecutor asked you what was the basis of this conclusion of yours. You answered because you have seen that before the war and during the war. Since you're an intelligent person, would you explain to the Court, how did you observe this link between the SDS party and the 4th Detachment? Could you explain this to the Court in greater detail, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the SDS leadership were all in the 4th Detachment. They were all together with the military. They remained in power when this military took over the power. So it was their army. That was my conclusion. And when the military entered Samac, when they took over the power, and they established this power, the same authorities and the same people remained -- the leadership of SDS remained. They remained on the same positions who were there, so this is really logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, here, you said to the Prosecutor that you had seen. I'd like to know, do you have direct information, or is that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've seen them together. They were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the municipal authority in 1992, also members from other parties were involved?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. Could you repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know the fact that also in the 4th Detachment, there were Muslims and Croats and Serbs in that unit?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How come that you, therefore, conclude, that the same people remain in power and that these others, as a military element, cooperate, when you had also people from the other parties in power as well as other ethnic -- representatives of other ethnic groups in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already how these Muslims came to be there, and I don't think I should repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that you've seen nothing in connection with that, that you've seen, and that this is your own personal conclusion, with no direct knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in any -- attend any political meetings when the circumstances were being discussed, and then conclude on the basis of that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you present in some military structures in order to come to such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, you have a rather non-defined position concerning this. You didn't directly participate or observe, so it's only your guesswork, your assumption.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this with my own eyes, all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, could you enumerate for me -- us the type of work you performed from the 17th of April, 1992, up to the moment of your exchange within the framework of your work duty?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from digging for bunkers in Grebnica, Lijeskovac, and Brvnik. Work in the separation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Explain what separation is, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a gravel pit, and we produced concrete elements with which then we built bunkers. It was from cement, gravel, and sand that we produced it, put it in moulds, and then built bunkers. We were separating the various -- and grading gravel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please be to the point. What else did you do?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the kitchen in Srpska Tisina. I did also agricultural work in Hrvatska -- Croatian Tisina, picking produce, vegetables. Then I went into the homes collecting things. I went also -- I worked -- I went by truck to Odzak and got wood. Then I went to Hrvatska Tisina to collect furniture and other objects from homes. Then I transported wood for shops, for private individuals. Then I worked one day in Hrana Produkt. I also went to Dubica within Odzak municipality, and there I brought -- collected certain items, and then we covered a roof for an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that is that.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also moved people -- helped in moving people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, I was thinking of the work.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I also unloaded planks, wooden planks, at the railroad station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, please do pause. And the Witness also, do wait for the translation to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, please count first to five, and only then answer. It's for the benefit of translation and transcript.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a directive?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, this is a request from the interpreters. So Mr. Hadzijusufovic, we will agree that when military conscript - and we are speaking of your knowledge - prior to the 17th of April, 1992, it means the preceding period, 1960's, 1970's, and 1980's in Bosnia, if you have the knowledge, because at the time you did serve your military service. So if a military conscript is not a member of the reserve forces of the army, he could be in the TO, in the civil protection, or have a work obligation. I'm asking you about your personal knowledge at that time on this.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on his physical ability to perform. He does not have to be in any of these, or maybe be placed in one of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the period of the conflict, 17th of April, 1992, armed conflict. One part of the population of Samac, including all nationalities, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, are on a series of locations as the military. They were called up from the reserve under a single command. They are on positioned on the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is his knowledge as to who was being called up? He is not a member of the military. He hadn't been in the military for years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But he is an eyewitness, Your Honours. He knows his neighbours, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not only is it called up -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He doesn't have to be a general or military expert. I'm asking about his personal knowledge whether a certain number of his neighbours were called up and were at the front. Simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's called up from the reserve under a single command, various nationalities. This is outside his expertise. This is outside his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, he said yes to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic. The Prosecution is given an opportunity to say what they want, please do not interrupt them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We should have an orderly way of proceeding with our trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is sustained, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, can we agree concerning the fact that --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your first words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I shall repeat. Can we agree that after the outbreak of conflict in April 1992, many civilians, women, and older people also, had a certain work obligation irrespective of their nationality? Somebody worked some positions, somebody worked in the fields, et cetera. Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, but you stated also during the cross-examination whether you knew certain people who had this work obligation, you said that you knew them. And how do you say you don't know anything?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand whom you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the inhabitants of Samac who had certain work obligation, which they performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which nationality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking of all nationalities. The work obligation applied only to two groups, and then Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you had no knowledge of the fact that Serbs had work obligations?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had none. They went and carried out their regular work in shops, but they didn't turn up and go in front of the retirement home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But some of the Muslims and Croats who were recruited and went to the front didn't have their work obligation?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge that the soldiers on the front, members of the army of Republika Srpska, were also digging trenches in order to reinforce their positions and fortify their positions?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was working at it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, when you were not working, you leave open the assumption that they were digging and fortifying their positions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How can we answer what was occurring when he was not working other than just speculate? And they are asking him to totally speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you hear from your friends or acquaintances --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I did not hear your first words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you hear from any acquaintances or neighbours who were in the front line via -- as the work obligation, or as soldiers, that the soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska were digging their trenches?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I neither asked nor was I interested in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, we can agree on one fact: You worked and carried out a series of jobs, performed a series of jobs, which you have enumerated, and these jobs per se are not discriminatory, are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't even know what that question means. I object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are. And I don't understand the question either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Neither do I, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Pantelic can explain, that the jobs are not discriminatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was going to say, you mean the jobs aren't discriminatory, the giving out, the selection of who does what is not discriminatory?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's a question of translation, but I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzijusufovic, do you find it wrong that you -- if you don't go in the army, go in the field in order to harvest and pick vegetables and the harvest? Is there anything bad in that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Explain to the Court what is wrong with that.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's wrong because I was forced to do it. I didn't go of my own free will. That's what's bad in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that in war, there's no free will; it is the -- a state that then determines who will serve the army and what has to be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object to that last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe it's put to him in the general course of events generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, his general knowledge, personal knowledge about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not in particular with --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, not in particular events. I'm asking him generally because he's an intelligent person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The events in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, your answer was "yes" with a comment. So you understood my question. So could we hear your comment.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard that front of a bunker between the two front lines, you have to mow grass, that that is an obligation. But that is what I had to do. That that would be my work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, we shall agree that you didn't do only that, you did a broad gamut of jobs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I was ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us explain something in the transcript of the 15th of April. You said the HDZ president was Mato Nujic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Mato.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mato Nujic, he worked in my company for some time. He was also the president of the municipality at some point, but I think it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Something else to be explained. You mentioned the village of Tramosnica. Whose village was that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a village in the Gradacac municipality populated by Catholic population, inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I would like to tender into evidence one map which was provided by the Prosecution to us. It's a map -- it's actually one part of the general map of -- its operational map of UNPROFOR issued in 1994 by military surveillance, I suppose. It's a part of the area of Bosanski Samac area, and I would like now to -- for this witness to make certain notes or remarks and lines with regard to the positions of his work obligation between the warring parties. Because he mentioned that in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Can we have copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, Prosecutor can check the map because it's only one copy, and then we shall put it on the ELMO, and then we shall tender it in evidence and make enough copy afterwards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished -- Your Honours, I really couldn't get my bearings on this map. I visited that village once. I visited during the war, and I passed through it once before the war. I don't think I'll be able to get my bearings on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. It's a little bit strange, because the witness hasn't even seen the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You described what the area is about. I think it's in answer of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think he thinks it's a street map of Tramosnica. It's not a street map. It's an area map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Because we are not speaking about specific town or village. We are speaking about the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzijusufovic, were you digging trenches in the region of the Tursinovac place? Do you know what I'm talking -- what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you give him time to look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: See whether or not he can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My understanding is he already found that on the map. So maybe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly take the marker and show us where you were digging the trenches, what was exact the location there. Could you draw a line. If it's difficult, just place an X at the place Tursinovac.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we have to move from the Sava bridge, Mosta Savi.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you find Bosanski Samac -- just a moment, Mr. Hadzijusufovic. Did you find Tursinovac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Place an X there, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tursinovac, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you dig trenches there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you pass through this village to the Sava River embankment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And look at Tursinovac, and the river is above it, as I see it.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I see it, it is below the village. Ormut, Grebinta [phoen]. I don't see the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You can see it is curving. You can see, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, this is Sava, as it is meandering.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So make a line where the trenches were.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Sava. Ormut. I cannot find the bridge on the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, you can see on the left like a railroad track going from Bosanski Samac towards Croatia, there is a bridge. Where else did you dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you pass through Tursinovac, and you go along the embankment, and I was digging along the way to Grebnica. Also an area called Ormut. I can draw that for you. I can use this map and draw for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are carrying on a conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot -- I cannot get my bearings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you dig trenches in Lijeskovac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It may be a simple solution. We're one minute from the break. Why don't we have him look at the map over the break, become familiar with it, and this could move much quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree absolutely. And I also would be in a situation to give a consent that the Prosecution can confer with the witness in that regard, that limited issue, during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it possible also for us to have copies of the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the Trial Chamber, of course. I have three copies. But my idea was after the -- his testimony, to make a copy with the marks, and then to be tendered into evidence and for the benefit of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but it's just better also for us to be following on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Three copies is for you, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take a break. We'll resume at 18.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you proceed with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzijusufovic, during the break, did you manage to find your way around this map?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you find the place called Grebnica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fine. Will you please make a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letters are long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Never mind. Just make a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you find Lijeskovac? If I can assist you, it's just below Grebnica?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you find Brvnik? It's slightly stretched below Lijeskovac. If you put it, the map on the ELMO, I can help you, perhaps. [In English] Just adjust the zoom, please. Good. Little bit small. [Interpretation] You see, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, down on the right when you're going from Lijeskovac, you see the letters B-R-V-N-I-K stretching like a snake?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, then it's to the right from Batkovic. The letters are stretched vertically.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fine. Make a circle around it and put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And now, please connect the line from Lijeskovac to Brvnik. Do you agree with me that was the front line?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you, and I understand this map very little. It's hard for me to say where I did my digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you dig at Brvnik?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I dug on the banks of the Sava below Tursinovac. When you're going from the bridge, people from Srpska Tisina were guarding that area. And if you are going from the Sava River, here is where the embankment started guarded by Serb forces. And this continues on towards the Grebnica road. I don't understand some things here. It says Bok, B-O-K, and there are a lot of things on this map that I don't quite understand. Srpska Tisina, the last house in that place continues and becomes Grebnica. I can't really find my way around this map. If you want me to draw anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because if the witness can't find his bearings on a map, then asking him to do the impossible is of no evidential value, because you can't hold him against whatever you -- he has expressed that several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only part you can see clearly is where the embankment on the Sava begins, and that's where I did some of the digging. First comes the Ormut field and then the Grebnica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you mark where the 4th Detachment was, on which side of the line?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the embankment -- I see the Sava River, but I can't really find it on this map. Ormut cannot be below Tursinovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have a lot of difficulties. Perhaps I should ask, what is the point of him marking on the map, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour. I would like to clarify the part of his statement with regard to the front line in the position of the Croatian army, Croatian Defence council army, and the 4th Detachment, just to be a part of his statement. Because he mentioned that during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, he did, but from what he says, he is unable to mark it on the map. So you stop using the map. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say the same thing. All he knows is where those cities are on that map. He can't find the particular locations which seems to be the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then I will proceed with another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we still have the map marked, for whatever it is worth. Can we have the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection from the Prosecution side, maybe we could have that tendered to the exhibit, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For identification, of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map will be treated as Document D30/1 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, we can agree, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, that within the framework of your work obligation you dug trenches on the Grebnica location?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bunkers and connecting trenches, yes. That's the name of that location, behind Tursinovac. First you have to go through all of Tursinovac before you get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We can then agree that you also dug the same connecting trenches in the area of Lijeskovac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And we can also agree that within your work duties, you also did your digging of trenches, connecting trenches and so on, in Brvnik?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was called, Brvnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the site where you worked, there were units of the Republika Srpska army, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, do you allow me to describe where individuals were standing and how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can do that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was digging at Brvnik and we were digging connecting trenches there, after digging bunkers, there were soldiers on that location from the following villages: Crkvina and Kruskovo Polje. One of the shift commanders named Stojan from Crkvina, who had been a truck driver before the war for the department store in Bosanski Samac, was wearing a uniform that consisted of camouflage trousers, a vest made of sheep skin but turned inside out. He had two ammunition belts across his chest making a cross across his chest. He had a fur hat on his head and a cockade on that fur hat. Another one also wore a fur hat with a cockade, and the others were also dressed in uniform, except perhaps for two or three men who had no uniform but only wore ribbons on their sleeves, whereas others had no insignia at all. When I was at Lijeskovac, there were no people from Samac at all. At Grebnica, the men wore camouflage clothing. Only a couple of them wore some emblems, and the others had no insignia or emblems at all, just camouflage uniforms. Hasim Dobichev's son, and Dumic, who was a mailman, had a cap with a cockade. That's all I saw on them, and I didn't mind them wearing that. Others didn't even have as much. That's all I had to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Hadzijusufovic, you have described the positions of the troops of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And on the other side, there were members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I learned later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that Samac was shelled?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where did the shells come from? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of -- this direction you mentioned, from the other side of Grebnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you also hear later that it was the HVO that shelled Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could make your own conclusions about the direction of the shells. I'm not an expert, but I can deduce it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, have you any knowledge about the fact that during the war in Samac, beginning with the 17th of April, 1992, until January 1993, that is the time that you spent in Samac, a large number of Muslims and Croats occupied various positions at the hospital and in other public services? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was a large number. But in the beginning, there were a couple who continued in their jobs, nurses, one woman doctor, Safet, Dr. Mesud, and one woman who worked in a shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in this period while you were in Samac, there was a rather large number of Muslims and Croats there with you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't quite understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there Croats and Muslims there during your stay in Samac from the 17th of April until January 1993?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any cases where a number of Croats and Muslims in that period, from April 1992 to January 1993, were taken to be exchanged but on the spot declined to go through with the exchange and returned and stayed in Samac until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of two such cases, the ones you mentioned before. And Ivan Lonac, who used to be a policeman, I think he had come back, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know these people personally?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Rado rather well, and I had another an acquaintance with the other. I believe both their wives were Serb. Even Lonac's wife is Serb for sure, and I can't tell you precisely about the other man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to speak with them after they had returned from the exchange?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Based on all that you have said, we will agree, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, that in that period that you spent in Samac from April 1992 to January 1993, there was basically no discrimination against the Croats and Muslims of Samac, because they continued working, and they had come back from this opportunity of exchange. They had to work, but there was no discrimination.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question at all. Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Muslims and Croats of Samac.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can you say there was no discrimination when they didn't allow us to go -- they forced us to go to forced labour. A moment ago when you asked the same question, I asked you, how can you not call it discrimination if I am forced to cut grass in front of the bunker? I didn't go to those works voluntarily. I had to go. And discrimination itself is implied if the camps were full, as they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you then answer, why did those Muslims and Croats come back to town from the line of exchange if there was discrimination in town? What is your position on this?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's their own problem. I learned later that in the case of Mijo Brada, he had come back because his wife and child -- the child was sick, and I don't know about the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that everybody could leave Samac if they wanted to do so, the only thing they had to do was report this wish to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How did you leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you ask to leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to relate one incident regarding all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In addition to what I have described, that I tried to register at least ten times and that my brother-in-law went to the office upstairs, my wife and I kept talking all the time and reckoning how to find a way out, how to get out of there. And then I remembered Cedo, the brother of this gentleman here. I was very close to him. We were on very good terms before the war. He had slightly injured me with -- when he hit me with his car. There was nothing too bad. And when the police came to investigate this incident, and if I wanted to press charges, I said no, because I wasn't really hurt. And I decided to go and see this man and ask him. That's what my wife and I decided to do. At first, I couldn't really find him. But then I found him outside the retirement home, and I approached him and begged him, please, you are my last chance. Please go to Cviko and register me for the exchange. You can do it, I know. You occupy a position, and I am aware that you are holding some sort of position. And he answered whatever I can do for you, I will. But he didn't do anything. My son got out by swimming across the river, and I absolutely disagree with you that it was so easy to get out, just to say that you wanted to be exchanged. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But nobody forced you to go; it was of your own free will that you put your name on those lists?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I wonder, just a small clarification, page 79, line 25, and the witness says, and then I remembered Cedo, the brother of this gentleman here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm wondering whether he's referring to you, Mr. Pantelic, or anyone else in the room. Maybe you can tell us exactly who you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain this, whose brother did you mean?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: ^Savic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Blagojevic. I cannot focus at this moment. I'm sorry. I mean Mr. Simic, Mr. Simic, sitting over there. I was referring to his brother Cviko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I don't have further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I have a question that you might be able to assist on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm looking at the exhibit that was put in this afternoon, Exhibit D34/3 ter. That's the summons to military duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. And you in your cross-examination have been talking about the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And on this summons, and I'll look at the ter copy in B/C/S, we have a stamp, and I think during Mr. Lukic's, I think, cross-examination, we were told by the witness that the stamp says Serbian republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Defence. Now, my question is this, and I have to obviously turn to the English version now: On the first page, it talks about summons, failure to answer it, shall be prosecuted under Article 79 of the law on military service and Article 214 of the Criminal Code. So my first question is, is that the former Yugoslavia's federal laws, or are these laws of the new Republika Srpska? And the second, and I think related, question, we go to the second page entitled "notes" which I believe also has the same stamp and date, which is 25th, August, 1992, we see in paragraph (c): "When summoned for military service in the JNA/Yugoslav People's Army ..." So I have a little confusion here. Republika Srpska army, JNA, former Yugoslavia's federal people's army, so if you could somehow try and clarify these points, I would be most grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Your Honour, that was a common, I would say, habit, with all three warring parties in Bosnia, with Croatian, Muslim, and Serbian. Because this was the old forms actually from former Yugoslavia. And practically, this article of law, the [indiscernible] and Criminal Code, referred to the former Penal Code of former Yugoslavia, SFRY. But it is the fact of common knowledge that they adopted legislation by Republika Srpska, certain laws adopted -- adopted all laws of former Yugoslavia, which was not contrary to their regime, et cetera, et cetera. So it is just I would say some kind of bypass because after these several months the Republika Srpska enacted other laws with regard to the Cyrillic alphabet, not Latinic, et cetera. The new forms. This is obviously -- it's a beginning of the creation of the Republika Srpska, so they practically used the old forms from JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So that would mean that when persons in the position of, for example, the witness here today received a summons for which there could be criminal penalties, the summons was summoning him or her to take up a position and that wasn't in existence, JNA, rather -- I won't say not in existence, but the summons was really for the army of Republika Srpska, and not for the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, it was the summons for Republika Srpska army, because you can see in the summons on the first page, in front of memorial hall, and then you have above this mentioning, you have VP, which means military post 6510 Bosanski Samac, which is actually the military post of Republika Srpska army, and then also I believe it was in May 1992, the law of defence was enacted, and then there are certain -- I would say provisions in that law with Republika Srpska which were related to the deserters, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it's a matter of evidence on which the Defence can call a witness during their case to explain the discrepancies. Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will be very brief. I have perhaps 20 questions all together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Hadzijusufovic.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief and to the point. I assume you're already tired.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, could you tell us whether -- are you any relation to Safija Hadzijusufovic of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a relative of all Hadzijusufovics in Bosanski Samac, but Safija -- she lived alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did she have a husband?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you cannot remember, let us continue, then. Mr. -- Sir, you were mentioning Mr. Subasic Jusuf.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He was the courier who would be telling you to go to your work duty, and he was a courier.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the organisation of the work brigade, Celic Dzevad was there also at the head of it, and he worked in your former company?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know what position did he hold, if you do know?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only gave the names of people who were supposed to go and work, the names of these people, depending on the type of job which had to be performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was he a clerk?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a go-between. A clerk a bit unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I will show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] D23/2. I would kindly ask the usher to put the English version on the ELMO, and the ter version before the witness, please. We don't have the English version yet. I'm sorry. Then just the Serbian version -- the ter version. I'm sorry. So it's Document D23/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at that document, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, and as it is the only copy, after reading it, if you would place it on the ELMO so that the Trial Chamber and all who are attending could have a look at it also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Would the usher be so kind just to adjust the zoom so we can see the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could ask you to read the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If it would be easier?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just for the benefit of other people in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Give it to the witness and let him read it out slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Payroll for clerks, typists, courier/messengers, couriers, who work on the organisation of work in the work brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under item number 2, under the clerks, we have Celic Dzevad. Under number 3, couriers, we have also the name of Jusuf Subasic, don't we?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzijusufovic, look at all these names, the persons, a total of nine. I apologise, the names. Look at the names. Do you know the people?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Seferdin, he together worked with me. Celic Dzevad. Efrudin had a university degree. He worked with me. Abdic Dzemal. I'm sure I know these people. I know Beriatalic [phoen], Mladic. Subasic Jusuf I do know. Kapetanovic, my neighbour, I do know. And I know this other colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you state of what ethnicity are they? Are they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I don't need this document any more. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us, Mr. Hadzijusufovic, during the testimony with the Prosecutor, you stated that while working duty, that you were injured, that you injured your leg, that something fell on your foot?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion -- on the question of the Prosecutor who asked whether you contacted a doctor, you answered, "No, because I was afraid."

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A few minutes ago, to a question of colleague Pantelic, you answered whether you know that the medical team in the health centre of Bosanski Samac was mainly -- this medical team, personnel, were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said Dr. Mesud, and Dr. Safet's daughter, Safet's daughter were also a doctor there. These are the two people. And Pop, that was a nickname of a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now I will show you a document and I will ask you to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... D22A/2 ter, and the English translation on the ELMO, please. Just one thing. I don't know whether it might be that it's under seal. It's under seal. Okay, then we won't need it -- it's under seal. I just saw the marking on it. So we're not putting it on the ELMO. Just give the 22A/2 ter to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you look at the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The heading is "The Health Centre of Bosanski Samac," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The title is "Data on Conditions, Methods, Means, for the Payment of Salaries on the Basis of Ratios Established for May 1992," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The first person is Dr. Nogic Mesud, and it says the chief gynecologist. I will read and you just confirm, please.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Second, Dr. Brdar Ruza, pediatrician?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Third, Hercinovic, Dr. Damir, general practitioner, Damir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Damir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under four, Azira Hadzialijagic, a general practitioner, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Jusufovic Urija, general practitioner and emergency service chief, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After these five names, we have medical technicians, nurses, and drivers. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of the first five names I read of doctors, physician, of what ethnicity are they?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four are Muslims, of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And Dr. Urija was a Croat, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see that the entire medical team were of Muslim or ethnicity, isn't it so? Of Muslim or --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Muslim or Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are thinking of the first five?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first five are physicians, doctors that is our [in B/C/S]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that at the time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew for those two I have mentioned before. I didn't know for the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reason to be afraid of these doctors?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never afraid of doctors I attend, but on that occasion, I didn't dare go. I wasn't afraid of doctors, but I was afraid of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify, you weren't afraid of the doctors, but of the health centre?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Could I explain it? I'll be short. Because Serbian, as I heard, injured Serbs and Serbian soldiers would come here for their checkups, and I believed that it would be better for me not to go there. That was my personal opinion and my personal position concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I was reminded by the registry that the document which is under seal, but the names were read out. So I was wondering whether the reason for the document being under seal is that the names were protected?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not one of the names which this witness has read. The name which is -- because the document is under seal is, I believe under number 9 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the name --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I read only the first five. I was cautious about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday during your testimony and when questioned by my colleague, you stated that the work obligation was applied practically only to Muslims and Croats. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that, my colleague Lukic mentioned some names of people who worked with you in the separation plant. Isn't this so?
